vulnerability.title: Symfony YAML parser recurses without a depth limit on nested blocks, sequences and mappings, allowing stack exhaustion

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.4.52 Parser.php tracks depth through ParserState::enterNestingLevel()/leaveNestingLevel() around parseBlock(), and Inline::parseSequence()/parseMapping() take the shared ParserState and enter a nesting level; v5.4.45 has none of this and no ParserState.php

fix_commits.message: [Yaml] Bound recursion depth in the parser

severity.numeric_level_rationale: The CNA CVSS 4.0 base is 8.2 High (availability only) and NVD Primary CVSS 3.1 is 7.5 High, but the GHSA page and OSV database label are Low and the OSV vector uses VA:L with E:U. The canonical severity keeps the CNA 4.0 vector and records every published score.
severity.source: GitHub_M CNA CVSS 4.0 metric; NVD also carries a Primary CVSS 3.1 7.5 High from nvd@nist.gov
severity.ghsa_label_note: The GHSA page labels the issue Low and OSV database_specific.severity is LOW with CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:U, while the CNA metric is 8.2 High with AT:P/VA:H. The split is material and recorded as published.

vulnerability.category_l2: Unbounded recursion / stack exhaustion in YAML parsing of untrusted nested structures

critical_operation.description: Parser::parseBlock() instantiates a fresh Parser and delegates to doParse(), so each nested block level begins with an empty parser object and no depth counter is carried across levels. The block parser reaches parseBlock() recursively on nested sequences and mappings, and Inline::parseSequence()/parseMapping() likewise recurse into each other for inline forms without any bound. A crafted YAML document with deeply nested mappings or sequences therefore drives recursion until the PHP stack is exhausted and the worker crashes. At v5.4.45 there is no ParserState.php and no maxNestingLevel at all; v5.4.52 introduces a shared ParserState with a default limit of 128 and enterNestingLevel()/leaveNestingLevel() in both the block and inline parsers.

entry_point.description: An application calls Yaml::parse()/parseFile() on attacker-controlled YAML, e.g. user-supplied configuration, fixtures or import data.

trace.description: doParse() recurses into parseBlock() for nested sequence entries
parseBlock() creates a new Parser with no inherited depth state and calls doParse() again
Inline::parseSequence() recurses into parseSequence()/parseMapping() for nested inline forms

location.verification_method: Static read of Parser.php and Inline.php at v5.4.45 and v5.4.52, the fix patch, tag peels and ancestry; no YAML document was parsed and no stack exhaustion was triggered.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No YAML document was parsed and no stack exhaustion was timed; the recursion depth is established statically.
The CVE record lists no fix commit SHA; 914f427e is identified from the 5.4.52 tree and its commit message, not from a CVE reference.
The 5.4.52 fix is stacked: ParserState.php is introduced by 914f427e, and sibling hardening commits (e77391b2 alias bounds, 9749cd43 regex hardening) follow it.
CNA 4.0 8.2 High and NVD 3.1 7.5 High disagree with the GHSA/OSV Low label and VA:L vector.
open_questions: The exact nesting depth required to exhaust a default PHP stack was not measured.
Non-5.4 branches were not diffed; only the 5.4 tags were inspected.
